coordinator.narrative: Bangladesh needs a flood warning for 2026-07-04, when combined projected inflow is 44,475 m3/s, above the 44,000 m3/s flood threshold, providing about one day of lead time from today. India contributes most on the warning date at 23,244 m3/s, followed by Nepal 6,940 m3/s, China 6,709 m3/s, Myanmar 4,312 m3/s, and Bhutan 3,270 m3/s. No single nation could identify this threat because each observed flows below its own local danger level and issued no local alert; the risk appears only when all five inflows converge in Bangladesh. For 2026-07-05, the reported combined inflow is 38,510 m3/s, but this is a lower bound because only four nations report, while the 8,311 m3/s on July 6 and 8,557 m3/s on July 7 are also incomplete lower bounds.
coordinator.recommendation: Immediately activate a coordinated July 4 flood-readiness operation—issue public warnings, pre-position evacuation and relief resources in exposed districts, and require rapid upstream updates to clarify the incomplete July 5–7 outlook.
